column1: # Known differences of Wine from Windows for the Windows test programs (dm/host/tests/run_wine_tests.sh). Columns: test (the run's name in host_tests.tsv or
# host_scripts.tsv), kind, check, evidence, reason, versions: the Wines the row holds for, each the first word of its `wine --version` (wine-9.0, wine-11.0), space-separated,
# or any; a row applies only under a Wine it names (a row of another Wine is neither a DIFFERS nor a NOT RUN), and its reason quotes that Wine's source or behaviour.
# kind differs: a FAIL or TIMEOUT of the test is reported as DIFFERS when every failed check of its log (a line of the test's output with FAIL or a cross mark) contains
#   the check text of one of the test's differs rows whose evidence (a fixed string, - for none) is in the log too; check - with an evidence: a run that failed with no failed
#   check line (a crash, a time-out) and shows the evidence. Any other failure stays a FAIL. A row's reason names the Windows API and what Wine does instead, with the
#   evidence (a minimal reproduction, Wine's own fixme line, Microsoft's documentation); a defect of the port's code that Windows would show too never goes here.
# kind not-run: the test is not started under Wine (check and evidence -): it cannot run there for a reason that is not Wine's behaviour (the reason says which).

column3: adjustable snapshot carries the host time zone
column5: _tzset: Wine's ucrtbase keeps only the first two letters of TZ's zone name (a reproduction with TZ=UTC gives _tzname[0] "UT", with PST8PDT "PS" and "PD"), where Microsoft's _tzset documents the three-letter name (TZ=PST8PDT: _tzname[0] "PST"); hle_time.c copies tzname[0] into the snapshot (Wine 11.0: dlls/msvcrt/time.c _tzset, lstrcpynA(_tzname[0], tz, 3), which keeps two characters and the terminator)

column3: lacks host allocations importable as pool buffers
column5: vkGetPhysicalDeviceExternalBufferProperties for VK_EXTERNAL_MEMORY_HANDLE_TYPE_HOST_ALLOCATION_BIT_EXT: through Wine's winevulkan, lavapipe reports no features and no compatible handle types (0, 0) while it lists VK_EXT_external_memory_host; the same query on the same lavapipe natively reports it importable (features 0x4, compatible 0x80). So no device meets the baseline (vk_device.c) and the t_vk_* programs that need one skip (Wine 9.0: dlls/winevulkan/vulkan.c wine_vkGetPhysicalDeviceExternalBufferProperties zeroes the properties; Wine 11.0 passes the query to the driver: dlls/win32u/vulkan.c get_physical_device_external_buffer_properties, and the import works there)
